Hi Karthik / Marissa,

FinSecure (prospect, security contact Asha Reddy copied below) sent a concise list of asks after last week's call. They need two capabilities to close:

1) Per-tenant configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days + custom). They want tenant-level toggles with an API to set and an audit trail (who changed what, when).
2) Ability to pin a tenant's data to a specific region (US-east / US-west) with enforced egress prevention — i.e., no cross-region backups for pinned tenants.

They also want an emergency data removal API (admin-initiated complete purge) and a corresponding compliance attestation (signed PDF) when executed. I've attached their short SOW and a spreadsheet of minimal retention requirements.

Can you confirm the following so I can get back to them with a timeline?
- High-level feasibility and major engineering gaps (approx dev weeks).
- Backwards compatibility implications (what existing customers might need to opt-in/out of).
- Any telemetry or storage-layer constraints (e.g., current blob store replication that would block regional pinning).
- An initial roadmap ask: can we target a gated beta in Q3 2027?

Asha is pushing for a firm date because this is a conditional part of their procurement. If we can provide a short bulleted answer by EOD Thursday (02/11), I can move this forward.

Thanks —
Irene
Director, Strategic Accounts

On Wed, Feb 10, 2027 at 9:12 AM Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com> wrote:
> FinSecure (prospect, security contact Asha Reddy copied below) sent a concise list of asks after last week's call. They need two capabilities to close:
>
> 1) Per-tenant configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days + custom). They want tenant-level toggles with an API to set and an audit trail (who changed what, when).
> 2) Ability to pin a tenant's data to a specific region (US-east / US-west) with enforced egress prevention — i.e., no cross-region backups for pinned tenants.

Thanks for the clear brief. Quick technical readout from infra/serving side:

- Retention windows: we currently have a cluster-level TTL and a logical tenant label, but not tenant-enforced lifecycle policies. Implementing per-tenant TTLs will require changes at the metadata layer (tenant policy table), retention worker that enforces per-blob TTL, and a replay-safe purge path. Rough estimate: 6-8 engineer-weeks to build MVP (policy CRUD API, background enforcer, audit events).

- Regional pinning: today our object store is multi-region replicated for durability. Preventing cross-region replication for a tenant requires either: (a) per-tenant placement constraints at provision time + separate buckets/replication rules, or (b) a logical encryption + key-homing approach (complicates KMS). Option (a) is more straightforward but will add operational burden (per-tenant buckets). Estimate: 8-12 engineer-weeks plus infra automation to provision region-scoped storage and backup exclusion.

- Emergency purge API: doable but must guarantee eventual consistency and retention of audit logs (we should not delete audit trail records). Implementation: 2-3 engineer-weeks to add an authenticated admin endpoint + purge worker + signed attestation generation.

Risks / follow-ups:
- Migration path for existing tenants: we need a migration tool to move tenant data from global buckets to region-scoped storage without downtime — non-trivial, estimate +4 weeks for a robust tool.
- Compliance attestation: product should generate a signed PDF with a unique reference ID; operations will need a playbook for audit review.

If we sequence this work: retention MVP -> emergency purge -> region pinning (with migration tooling), we can aim for a gated beta in Q3 if we staff 2-3 engineers full time. If not, timeline slips to late Q3/early Q4.

I'll prepare a short tech note and risk list for the roadmap meeting.

—Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
